verdict.rationale: Missive's own MCP server lets external AI agents act on conversations, contacts, calendar and drafts "with the permissions you choose," so it has a first-party, permission-scoped way to grant agent access. The evidence is one changelog line, with no detail on how credentials are issued, how fine-grained scopes are, or whether REST API tokens can be scoped. The MCP-client auth options and API-key swaps cover Missive connecting to other services and are not credited here. Missing for 10: documented scoped API token issuance for the REST API, a granular scope/permission reference, per-agent credential management and revocation, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: External AI apps like Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor can now connect to Missive through the Model Context Protocol and act on your conversations, contacts, calendar, and drafts, with the permissions you choose.
official MCP server documented at https://missiveapp.com/docs/ai/mcp/server
